clue.text: Meiosis in T 'S Eliot play

indicators.note: to play with letters is to toy with them, so the poet's initials and surname are juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: Understatement in a drama by the poet T S Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a noun, a work by Eliot, but it is the anagram signal working on the seven letters of T S ELIOT. The page prints the name as T S Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: Meiosis is the rhetorical term for understatement, and the figure of affirming by denying the opposite is a specific type of it.

clue.text: Most reasonable to behold direction of bright land

parts.note: lo is the old exclamation meaning look or behold
from Clough's poem Say Not the Struggle: 'westward, look, the land is bright', so the compass point is west

explanation.surface: A traveller seeks the most sensible view towards a sunlit country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bright land' quotes Arthur Hugh Clough's poem, which ends 'But westward, look, the land is bright'. 'Most reasonable' is used of prices, as in the lowest offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasonable price is a modest one, so the most reasonable price is the cheapest or least.

clue.text: Land given to church for row of houses

parts.note: terra is Latin for land, used in English as in terra firma
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Ground is donated to the parish to build a street of homes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a terrace is a continuous row of houses joined side by side.

clue.text: But it is not related to the Dutch elm

definitions.text: But it is not related to the Dutch elm

parts.words: But it is not related to the Dutch elm
parts.note: the clue seems to be about elm disease or tree families; the joke is a tree named after the Dutch bulb flower that is in fact a magnolia relative, unrelated to elms or Holland

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that some tree has no kinship with the Dutch elm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' points at the bulb Holland is famous for; the North American tree with flowers shaped like that bulb is no elm.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American Liriodendron, called after its cup-shaped flowers, belongs to the magnolia family, not to the elms.

clue.text: Shooting-brake?

parts.note: a shooting-brake is an old British name for an estate car; read instead as something that brakes or stops shooting, it is the gun's locking lever

explanation.surface: Just a question about an estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting-brake is a British term for an estate car (station wagon); the question mark invites reading it as a brake on shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The locking device on a firearm prevents it being fired accidentally, literally putting a brake on shooting.

clue.text: Eg. Rosemary and Theo involved in Rossetti's group

indicators.note: in places the jumbled name inside the brotherhood's initials

parts.note: Dante Gabriel Rossetti co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, abbreviated PRB

indicators.note: involved here means tangled or convoluted, so the four letters of the name are twisted

explanation.surface: Two people, Rosemary and Theo, have joined the Pre-Raphaelite circle of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a woman's name paired with Theo, but it is the herb; the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood signed its early paintings with the initials PRB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a culinary herb, an example of a plant grown for the kitchen pot.

clue.text: Make regular journeys in the Strand

definitions.meaning: to ... a route is to travel it regularly, as a ferry does
a strand of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: Commuting back and forth along the famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street, a natural place for buses to run, but here it is a thread of wool or rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat or bus works a route by travelling it to and fro, and one twisted thread of a yarn is its layer.

clue.text: Some of his Aminta's so pastoral

definitions.text: Some of his Aminta's so pastoral

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, so the poet's name lies within the run of letters

explanation.surface: Much of this author's Aminta is very rural in mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Aminta (1573) is a pastoral drama by the Italian Renaissance poet, so the whole clue both describes him and contains him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian poet Torquato wrote the pastoral play Aminta, so 'his Aminta' identifies its author.

clue.text: English law expert and poet

parts.note: a legist is a specialist in law

explanation.surface: Someone is both an English lawyer and a writer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of mournful laments for the dead is a type of versifier.

clue.text: Sike's pet sweetmeat

definitions.meaning: Bill Sikes in Dickens's Oliver Twist owns a dog called ...
a round hard peppermint-flavoured boiled sweet

explanation.surface: A villain's dog is a confection.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Oliver Twist; his bull terrier shares its name with a striped British boiled sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens named Sikes's dog after the target centre, and a hard mint candy with the same name is a confection.

clue.text: Cause of lumps in a jersey?

definitions.text: Cause of lumps in a jersey?

parts.words: Cause of lumps in a jersey?
parts.note: a jersey seems to be a knitted pullover, but a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, whose hide swells where this insect's larvae burrow

explanation.surface: Asking why a knitted pullover has gone lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jersey is a dairy-cattle breed from the Channel Island; the insect's larvae form swellings under cattle hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The botfly Hypoderma lays eggs on cattle and its larvae raise lumps called warbles under the skin.

clue.text: Splendid organ-effect

definitions.meaning: an old slang adjective meaning excellent
a mechanism on a pipe organ that varies loudness by opening shutters

explanation.surface: Praising a fine sound from the church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Swell is dated slang for first-rate, and the organ's swell box gives crescendo effects.

clue.text: Die to make an impression

definitions.meaning: a die is a tool for striking a design onto metal or paper
to press a mark into something

explanation.surface: Advice that dying is one way to make your mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' looks like a verb, to perish, but it is the noun for a striking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal punch that imprints a design is the device, and pressing that design into a surface is the action.

clue.text: Art of constructing moving rock Masses, say

definitions.meaning: the science of building and design
the study of shifting plates of the earth's crust, as in plate theory

explanation.surface: The craft of building with heavy shifting stone blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses' with its capital seems to mean church services, but it is plain mass of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the art of building, and in geology it means the study of crustal plate movement.

clue.text: Girl perhaps exciting crowd with pair of hips for a start

definitions.text: Girl perhaps exciting crowd with pair of hips for a start

parts.words: Girl perhaps exciting crowd with pair of hips for a start
parts.note: the girl seems to sway her hips to excite the crowd; in fact 'hip hip' begins the hooray, and she leads the shouting

explanation.surface: A young woman wiggles her hips to stir up the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of hips is the 'Hip, hip' that starts a 'Hooray', led by the girl with pompoms at a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad member who leads the crowd's chants and shouts at games, often a young woman.

clue.text: Composition of rocks for some, pretty rich model

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so these letters are reshaped into the answer

explanation.surface: A model, quite rich, describes geology to some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun, a fashion model who is pretty and rich, but it is the anagram signal working on SOME plus PRETTY RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemistry of rocks and minerals is the study of their makeup.

clue.text: Lady Smitton, we hear, in Italy

definitions.text: Lady Smitton, we hear, in Italy

parts.words: Lady Smitton, we hear, in Italy
parts.note: Smitton sounds like smitten; the Italian word for a lady who is smitten or in love, borrowed into English, means a sweetheart

explanation.surface: An aristocrat named Lady Smitton is rumoured to be in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Smitton looks like a society name, but say it aloud: a smitten lady, which in Italy is innamorata, giving the English loanword for a beloved woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with whom someone is in love; the loanword comes from Italian for enamoured.

clue.text: Last of "Pussycat" represents Edward L. as nonsense-writer

indicators.note: only the final letter of the quoted word is taken
to represent is to present anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The final word on the Pussycat goes to Edward Lear, the nonsense poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse including The Owl and the Pussycat, so the surface's poet is also the definition's kind of writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks or writes twaddle produces silly drivel.

clue.text: The nerve of Thomas Percy — such bottle!

definitions.text: The nerve of Thomas Percy — such bottle!

parts.words: The nerve of Thomas Percy — such bottle!
parts.note: Thomas Percy was Earl of Worcester in Shakespeare's Henry IV; the earl's nerve or cheek is his sauce, and bottle is a container for the condiment

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at the courage of a historical nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce and bottle are both British slang for cheek and nerve; Thomas Percy, Earl of Worcester, rebels in Henry IV, Part 1. The condiment is sold in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy British condiment from Worcestershire, here read as an earl's impudence.

clue.text: This towelling is friction-reduced

parts.note: a rub is an act of friction
down means lowered or reduced, as in prices down

explanation.surface: Drying with a towel cuts down on friction.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk massage or drying with a towel after exercise or a bath.

clue.text: Amerind Watch Co gone bust

indicators.note: a bust firm has broken up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Native American clock company has gone bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: Amerind is an old term for an American Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people originally from the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Enthusiastic rating

definitions.meaning: a rating is a non-commissioned sailor, a jolly seaman of 'me hearties'

explanation.surface: A keen review score.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a naval sailor below officer rank, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means vigorously cheerful, and old sea talk calls sailors 'my hearties'.

clue.text: His policy is to go in for huge excesses

definitions.text: His policy is to go in for huge excesses

parts.words: His policy is to go in for huge excesses
parts.note: reads like a politician's spending plans, but describes a man given to dissipation

explanation.surface: Someone's strategy is to make enormous overspends.
explanation.walkthrough: Policy and excesses suggest finance; the man described simply indulges every appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: A man devoted to sensual excess and dissipation.

clue.text: Riding-school accident

parts.note: a pupil thrown from a horse is overturned; the word also means any mishap

explanation.surface: A mishap at a stable teaching horsemanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown or overturned, a mishap or spill.

clue.text: Love area of bracing air

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Adoring a region of fresh invigorating breezes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popularly, if inaccurately, the name for fresh seaside air.

clue.text: Reverse reel features curved figures

indicators.note: reverse sends the word for a reel back to front

parts.note: a spool is a reel for winding thread or film

explanation.surface: A film shown backwards features curved shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapes that bend round to cross themselves, such as those made by skaters or stunt planes.

clue.text: Wild dream that produced a progressive party-leader

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A crazy vision gave birth to a forward-looking political chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The party is the Mad Tea-Party in Alice in Wonderland, where the guests keep moving round the table, so its host is progressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's tea-party host keeps everyone shifting seats, so he leads a party that moves on.

clue.text: More, say, for one of the greedy guts

indicators.note: say tells us to use the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: the word more said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Asking for more is typical of a glutton.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech 'more' has no final R sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The maw is the stomach or gullet, especially of a voracious animal.

clue.text: Game in which one. can lose one's marbles, being knocked out

definitions.text: Game in which one. can lose one's marbles, being knocked out

parts.words: Game in which one. can lose one's marbles, being knocked out
parts.note: losing one's marbles is going mad, but in this game players knock marbles out of a ring

explanation.surface: A contest so punishing that one goes mad from being knocked unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'one can'; the held text has a stray full stop after 'one'. Players shoot a taw at marbles in a ring to knock them out.
explanation.definitionFit: A marbles game played by shooting at marbles in a ring.

clue.text: The place for vehicles when theatreland has black-out

indicators.note: out means the letter for black is removed from the theatre street

parts.note: Broadway in New York is the heart of American theatre
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Traffic takes over the streets when the theatre district has a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black-out' suggests a power cut, but 'black' gives B and 'out' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The carriageway is the part of a street for traffic.
